reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess whether tisseel fibrin sealant engaged fibrinogen. The mechanism involves fibrin polymerization for hemostasis, but no direct target engagement measurements were reported. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers or pharmacodynamic markers were measured to confirm that fibrinogen engagement led to enhanced fibrin polymerization and hemostasis. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (post-operative wound drainage volume) clearly failed in both anatomical sites. Groin dissection showed 892.5 ml vs 762.5 ml (p=0.704) and axillary dissection showed 565 ml vs 590 ml (p=0.217). Neither reached statistical significance. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial tested two different anatomical sites (groin vs axillary lymph node dissection) but both failed, suggesting no subgroup benefit. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial appears adequately powered with 74 patients and appropriate controls. No obvious confounders identified.

failure_modes.evidence: While no biomarkers were measured, the fibrin sealant mechanism is well-established and likely engaged (fibrin polymerization for hemostasis), but this did not translate to reduced wound drainage volume in either anatomical site tested
